# Half Hourly Insights

> A free tool for analysing UK half-hourly (HH) electricity meter data. Load one Excel or CSV file per meter and see out-of-hours use priced at your rates, base load, peaks against agreed supply capacity, unusual days and lasting changes, with savings scenarios, PDF and Excel reports and password-protected customer dashboards.

Operated by Kinetic Energy Consulting. Free to use, no sign-up. The analyser runs entirely in the browser: meter data is never uploaded.

Scope: UK businesses and public sector organisations. Results are indicative estimates from the data loaded: costs are energy cost at the rates entered, not guaranteed savings, and whole-site data shows when energy is used, not which equipment uses it. The method is set out on the How it works page.

Method in brief: base load is the 5th percentile of valid half-hourly demand; out-of-hours (closed-hours) excess is energy used outside the opening hours above that base load; missing readings are left out, never counted as zero; annual figures are scaled from valid hours and withheld under 180 days of data; kVA is kW divided by an assumed power factor.

## Tool

- [Analyser](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/analyser/): the tool itself, in the browser.

## Core pages

- [Half Hourly Insights: free business electricity data analysis](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/): What the analyser shows, the three steps, and the privacy model (analysis runs in the browser).
- [How it works](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/how-it-works.html): The method in full: reading files, data checks, opening hours, base load (5th percentile), closed-hours excess, costs, annualisation, findings, capacity, and limits.
- [Questions and answers](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/faq.html): Cost, privacy, the data needed and what the results mean.
- [Contact](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/contact.html): Enquiries to Kinetic Energy Consulting, which runs the site.
- [Sample electricity report for an office](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/sample-report.html): A sample report for a made-up office: 33% of use while closed, £2,776 a year above base load, base load 2.6 kW, findings and what could be saved.

## Guides

- [How to get your half-hourly electricity data](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/get-your-data.html): Who holds half-hourly data, what to ask your supplier for, the file layouts the analyser reads, and what to do if your supplier cannot provide it.
- [Worked example: a year of half-hourly data for one office](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/example-office-analysis.html): A small office run through the analyser: 33% of use while closed, £2,776 a year above base load, almost half on Saturdays; base load 2.6 kW; 67% of a 40 kVA supply.
- [Out-of-hours electricity use: how to find and cut it](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/out-of-hours-electricity.html): What out-of-hours electricity use is, how to find it in half-hourly data (opening hours, heatmap, day types, start and end of the day), common causes, fixes and who to involve.
- [Base load electricity: what it is and how to cut it](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/base-load.html): What base load is, how to measure it from half-hourly data (5th percentile, not the minimum), what makes it up, how to reduce it; 1 kW all year is 8,760 kWh.
- [Supply capacity and kVA: room for heat pumps and EVs](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/supply-capacity.html): Agreed supply capacity in kVA, kW to kVA via power factor, headroom from half-hourly peaks with a safety margin, and checking heat pumps and EV charging.
- [Worked example: a primary school's half-hourly data](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/example-school-analysis.html): A primary school with term dates entered: 31% of use while closed, £1,261 a year above base load; heating left on through October half term (demand more than double); evening lettings.
- [How to read a half-hourly electricity heatmap](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/reading-a-heatmap.html): How to read a half-hourly heatmap (days across, time of day down, colour for demand) and the patterns that point to waste.
- [How to prove an energy saving worked, with half-hourly data](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/proving-savings.html): Proving a saving with half-hourly data: matched before-and-after periods, the right measure for the change, weather effects, and the analyser tools.
- [Market-wide half-hourly settlement (MHHS) explained](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/half-hourly-settlement.html): Market-wide half-hourly settlement: Ofgem decision 20 April 2021; migration began 21 October 2025, due complete 7 May 2027; four-month settlement timetable from 2 July 2027; microbusinesses cannot opt out.
- [Glossary of half-hourly electricity terms](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/glossary.html): Definitions: base load, closed-hours excess, kW, kWh, kVA, power factor, MPAN, agreed supply capacity, settlement, MHHS, heatmap, load factor and more.
- [Guides to half-hourly electricity data](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/guides.html): Index of guides.
